premise.claim: Issue #490: 'Patching a live Pod's status to Failed (test/utils.SetPodFailed) ... Pod status is owned by the kubelet, which rewrites the patched phase ... Either way the failure trigger can evaporate before the controller acts on it', causing intermittent timeouts / vacuous passes in the restart-backoff e2e specs.
premise.evidence: Tests-only PR (premise carve-out applies); mechanism verified on base: SetPodFailed/SetPodEvicted used rclient.Status().Update on live pods (8a7bcfcb:test/utils/utils.go:146-166), and kubelet owns pod status so a patched phase is transient. Issue #490 documents CI failures (runs 37258247385, 35559402297, 35751708068). Not reproduced locally: the live kubelet layer is out of scope this round.

findings.note: Backoff e2e specs lost the terminal-Failure trigger; the generation/revision bypass regression (instance_scale.go:413-416) is no longer detectable at the e2e layer. Green only when a backoff spec injects a terminal Failed Pod via buildFailingPodTemplate/failPod.
PR's own helper unit test: kubeconfig forwarding, verbatim args, error reporting.
Reviewer-added fixture contract: healthy until marker, exit code exactly 1 after marker, exit 0 on TERM.

match: should not freeze rolling update when revision mismatch occurs during backoff
should delay second recreation due to backoff
should only replace the failed pod, not recreate all pods
should recreate all pods when container RestartCount > 0
findings.note: Controller contracts the migrated e2e specs now rely on, guarded at the envtest layer. Mutation evidence: removing the generation/revision bypass makes the freeze spec fail (results/mutation-bypass-removed.out) while the current head passes (results/mutation-bypass-restored.out).
